manifest_units.key_interpretation: MSS EUR HODGSON/6 is currently the strongest candidate modern survival of at least part of 1864 item 12. The exact historical item number and matching content jointly exceed thematic coincidence, but direct BHH/11/14-BHH/19/5 comparison is required before calling it proven.

crosswalk_hypothesis: At least part of the modern vol.6/10/11 cluster may preserve or descend from the English-volume portion of Trunk No.2's second large bundle, while rough army scraps dispersed into vol.7/9. The 1921 size-based binding may have re-segmented these older transfer units.
falsification_tests: Read RAS BHH/11/14 and BHH/19/5 item 12 and compare wording/annotations against Hunter 1896.
Inspect the old leather/title layer of vol.6 to determine whether Box 2 / Item 12 is an 1864 transfer address or an earlier shipment address.
Inspect vol.10 for old cover/container labels; a matching Box/Item address would strengthen item 11 mapping.
Inspect all six vol.11 notebook covers for old numbers/bundle descriptions and test whether three historical English volumes can be reconstructed.
Compare physical dimensions and binding structures to see whether 1921 could have combined/split the old English volumes.
Locate Persian/Khas companion papers named in manifest item 12 and test whether modern cross-references converge on the same English states.
source_control_rules: Content overlap plus number match supports a high-confidence candidate but is not identical to diplomatic identity proof.
Do not collapse 'Trunk No.2', 'second large bundle', and Cambridge 'Box 2' into one hierarchy without physical list comparison.
The 1864 'three volumes' need not equal three modern 1921 volume numbers.
Modern vol.11's six pre-bound notebooks may be remnants of multiple historical volumes or a later combination.
Hunter 1896 is a downstream reproduction; event-near RAS list states outrank it once directly inspected.
